CS-01/final.text:
Hey - in humanize, `naturalsize` always prints one decimal place, so 3,000,000 bytes shows as "3.0 MB" and 1024 bytes with binary=True shows as "1.0 KiB". I'd like it to drop a trailing ".0" so those read "3 MB" and "1 KiB", but keep the decimal when it's meaningful (e.g. "2.9 KiB" should stay as it is). Can you implement that?

Thanks. Actually, I just realized that changing the default output is going to break a bunch of our templates and snapshot tests that expect "3.0 MB", and naturalsize is supposed to stay compatible with jinja2's filesizeformat. Please keep the default output exactly as it was before, and make the trailing-".0" trimming opt-in through a new keyword argument `strip_trailing_zero` (default False). Existing calls that pass a custom `format` string, including positional ones like naturalsize(3000, False, True, "%.3f"), must keep producing exactly what they produced before.

CS-02/final.text:
TinyDB's JSONStorage rewrites the database file in place (seek to 0, write, truncate), so if the process dies or the disk fills up in the middle of a write, the JSON file is left half-written and the whole database becomes unreadable. Can you make JSONStorage writes atomic - write the new contents to a temporary file and then swap it into place - so the file on disk is always either the old version or the new one?

Later in the session the user added:

Thanks! A few things I should have said up front: our app keeps a single TinyDB instance open for its whole lifetime and reads right after writing, so reads through the same instance (and the same storage object) must always see what was just written. Please also keep honoring the `encoding` argument and the extra json kwargs (like indent=4 or sort_keys=True) exactly as before, so the bytes written are the same as today. And don't leave temporary files lying around next to the database file - not after a normal write, and not when a write fails halfway (in that case the original file must stay exactly as it was).

Thanks. Two refinements: if the whole input is already in uppercase (like a shouted heading 'HELLO WORLD'), titleize should still produce 'Hello World' like it does today - only treat an all-caps word as an acronym when the input also contains lowercase letters.
